films.title: HOW TO BREAK OFF AN ENGAGEMENT

cues.text: What we've made, we don't want. What we've sold — to the world, to ourselves — doesn't exist. I look for a way out: through the hallways, within the drawers, and fire escapes.
The vape gathers, inside and out. My vision blurs. I move toward the window — and you only get further away. More haze.
It was the maze, constructed by a tainted love. You fall off the fire escape, into darkness — and the city streaks upward like it's leaving too.
cues.screen: IT WAS THE MAZE CONSTRUCTED BY A TAINTED LOVE

cues.text: I trip on my own words, falling out of life — and find where you go when you leave. The gap between us breathes, and never closes.
cues.screen: TRIP ON MY OWN WORDS - FALLING OUT OF LIFE
UNTIL IT GETS AS DARK AS BLACK
WHERE YOU GO WHEN YOU LEAVE - PART 2 OF 3: FUTURE

cues.text: It was the type of silent scream a trapped lover makes to escape: a pending marriage, a concussion, a set of walls caving inward.
cues.screen: A SET OF WALLS CAVING INWARD

cues.text: An emergency call while tossing and turning — the silent call a man makes to the mirror after midnight, to digest a truth.
cues.screen: TRYING TO SEE IN THE DARK

cues.text: A winless insomnia. An epiphany of a road winding down. My eyes dilate — and we go through.

I was six, I recall, when the ghost of a dead and love-less seven-year-old appeared, and shared that my parents' marriage wouldn't last. A warm, heavy breeze in winter, where a child is left home alone.
Curtains pulled, and blinds up as far and as wise as possible — to see flashing lights, and the whispering screams of two souls on a road winding down.
cues.screen: TWO SOULS ON A ROAD WINDING DOWN

cues.text: And no tears, and no fucks, and no love to give. The ghost hands me a tambourine — and I throw it through the window.
cues.screen: NO TEARS - NO LOVE TO GIVE
HOW TO BREAK OFF AN ENGAGEMENT

cues.text: Ode to forever — a tambourine sounds off an empty temple, empty choir stands, empty prayer lines.
And abandoned baptism pools. It flies in through the rose window — still whole.
Pews taken by cobwebs, and doused in disintegration. Spirits have left salvations in opened gift boxes, placed outside the side doors.

It thunders. Then rains until nothing remains. What was once love, now goods — broken and sealed apart by lightning. Daily breads, soaked and delivered rotted by rain; and blankets, soiled by venomous puppeteers.
Ode to the storm ending. Ode to two sets of mud-imprinted footsteps, leading away from what the water kept.
cues.screen: ODE TO TWO SETS OF MUD-IMPRINTED FOOTSTEPS

cues.text: And a tambourine, shattered into pieces. What if I followed this trail, to where the broken pieces have washed ashore?
cues.screen: AND A TAMBOURINE SHATTERED INTO PIECES

cues.text: What if I followed this trail, to where the broken pieces have washed ashore — and the ashes of expired wildfires cover sands, and debris lifted from the night sea water's floor.
cues.screen: WHERE THE BROKEN PIECES HAVE WASHED ASHORE

cues.text: The waves calm to folded whispers; the winds mute the trees. The right level of silence, to find a throbbing heart — it used to be mine. I lift it with care: nevermore.
What if I followed this reclaimed heart, to where the puzzle pieces of faith are handcrafted — scrambled and scattered as mustard seeds into the vast moonlit night's garden fields.

The plants in a golden hue bloom, and face toward me in anticipation. The weeds repel, falling into the shadows where our memories hide — and mean so little, in a moment of defeat — as I'm called forward.
cues.screen: THE PLANTS IN A GOLDEN HUE BLOOM, FACED TOWARD ME

cues.text: The clouds mute the stars for the deepest level of darkness — welcoming extra hard work, to search the bare ground for two hands.
cues.screen: TO SEARCH THE BARE GROUND FOR TWO HANDS

cues.text: Hands that once could touch dust after dusk, and feel good — they too used to be mine. I put them back on, with the care of my future at stake: nevermore.
cues.screen: THEY TOO USED TO BE MINE

cues.text: Now go, they tell me. To ask if I can inherit the earth — to ask if I can name my own stars. Even galaxies, if I may.
cues.screen: TO ASK IF I CAN NAME MY OWN STARS

cues.text: The past, too, was waiting for me — coming of age in the shared rooms of humid basements as bedrooms; mattress pads where the wood beams of Southern pine could comfort my spine. It didn't. To dream was to prevail.
They tell me: ask if I can invent a new universe — if God would let me, little ole me, award a blessing here and there. Even grant miracles.
cues.screen: TO ASK IF I CAN INVENT A NEW UNIVERSE

cues.text: In uncertain times, in forsaken times. Their blood flows through my hands — fingerprints that orchestra great powers — sun-kissing my skin, deepening my voice to a baritone of a million cries. Beware of me.
The gates open with wings — gifted from evolution, and made of marble stones kissed by the hymns our Creator composed, with an orchestra of our ancestors' wildest dreams, to welcome us.
cues.screen: KISSED BY THE HYMNS OUR CREATOR COMPOSED

cues.text: Poets, who eased generations down yellow brick roads — and plucked our souls out of their secret places, to follow comets to the capital city of our collective consciousness.
cues.screen: TO FOLLOW COMETS TO THE CAPITAL CITY

cues.text: Resurrecting Atlantis. Here we are all one — the pact we've made here with nature, abandoned and hoped for the best, back on life.
A relearned currency, we reassess as the admission. But here we are all safe. An unfamiliar, flickering candle light, illuminating smiles at night.
cues.screen: A RELEARNED CURRENCY, WE REASSESS AS THE ADMISSION

cues.text: Where shadows cast from narrow streets beaming with love — in the joyful noises that color rainbows, and give us infinite time to heal, and set clouds free.
I know my soul — and it could stay here forever. Leaving behind crosshairs for continuums, and strains for serendipity.
cues.screen: I KNOW MY SOUL, AND IT COULD STAY HERE FOREVER

cues.text: A city born in unison, out of the purest of fictions — welcoming me, and welcoming all.
cues.screen: A CITY BORN IN UNISON OUT OF THE PUREST OF FICTIONS

cues.text: DJ, turn me up, please. Eyes wide shut, chin nested at the arch of the weight of these spoken words.
I have a love story to tell — of ghosts, whispering unfolded dilutions, birthed in purity, and dying in the vineyards of sun-soaked evergreen fields, unnourished.
cues.screen: I HAVE A LOVE STORY TO TELL

cues.text: One by one, treasures escaping — devaluing themselves after unsullied stars diminished their glares. I walked a thousand light years to be heard. So DJ — please — turn me up.

So I can speak: of wedding bands diverging across abstract skies of wounded souls. Of a shared home, boxed and trucked on separate one-way streets — not built with U-turns, or stop, maybe-we-shouldn't signs.
A love story of years — eleven years — each plunkled off as daisy petals. We love, we not. Of a future gone swiftly, and a past left empty-handed.
To pick a road: of heavy rain. Or of frontal fog. Or of dimmed night lights under a cloud — with a silver lining.
Now, turning forth to face delights and shadows — one night at a time; one tear at a time; one open mic at a time. Chin now nested high, and volume turnt up.
Pulsing, and head throbbing from the music — and empty, on a crowded floor of sweated perfumes and temptations.
cues.screen: A CROWDED FLOOR OF SWEATED PERFUMES

cues.text: The soul escapes my body, and leaves him on the dance floor — just flesh and bones. Rejection and heartache hit different, with no feelings afloat.
cues.screen: HE CAN NOW JUST BE FLESH AND BONES

cues.text: I want my soul to imagine my body. Watch strangers collide and spark electric currents that gamut the mood. We want him to be the last to leave.
Now let us put my soul in the middle of an open field — at the equator of a planet much larger than my own, and much hotter.
cues.screen: A PLANET MUCH LARGER THAN MY OWN

cues.text: Cool me down: pouring unfiltered water out of ice baths, salted from the closest moons, from angles of the newest religions — their graces curse or bless me. Only infinity will tell.
Now bring my soul back to my body: to lean back, breathe in the smoke that fills the room — how good it is to finally get acquainted with the night.
Unfamiliar, yet relatable mountains in the distance; wandering thoughts within reach. Accepting you'll never say, nor feel, my love was real. What isn't mine, I still can not give.
cues.screen: WHAT ISNT MINE, I STILL CAN NOT GIVE
WHAT ISN'T MINE, I STILL CAN NOT GIVE.

cues.text: Before I go, we look at the moon the way we used to see it. We talk for years, travel through time — we grow old together, I believe. Maybe we could have it all.
cues.screen: WE TALK FOR YEARS AND TRAVEL THROUGH TIME

cues.text: Before I go, I call on my mother — in tears, speaking of an abyss she's never known. We talk for years, re-closet wounds, and re-explain my way of birth. Even after prayer: what isn't mine, I still can not give.

Before I go, I call on my father — his calming demeanor summoned from the yonders. We walk for years, east toward the sunrises, retracing his footsteps — my tears falling in the wave shadows of the inner harbor.
We stroll, father and son, hearted and shaken. Someone borrowed, and someone blue — yet, broken. Yet, heard.

cues.screen: I WASN'T LOOKING FOR A RIDE

cues.text: I wasn't looking for a ride, but here you are — blissful, and oddly sensitive. I rub my aggressions into your steel coverings, and hop on.
cues.screen: I WASN'T LOOKING FOR A RIDE, BUT HERE YOU ARE

cues.text: Loneliness is having everything with no one to tell — being everywhere, with no one to love. I let the noise block the noise. The way I ride: eyes turn, heads twist — and prove the magic still exists.
cues.screen: I LET THE NOISE BLOCK THE NOISE

cues.text: All preparations to live and dream in darkness, I no longer desire. The moon settles, and the tease of distant stars subsides — and I can see a morning ahead for me.
cues.screen: THE TEASE OF DISTANT STARS SUBSIDES

cues.text: It looks like a morning I could believe in — a morning where loss and life aren't so — well — ripe with sunlight that's deceptively warm. The chirping of birds, fueling of nests, spring out of the night that has covered me.
cues.screen: A MORNING I COULD BELIEVE IN

cues.text: With my own curiosities, for a chance at an end wherever everything will be OK. I want to live in this feeling forever — blissful, and oddly innocent.
cues.screen: EVEN HERE, IT'S CHILLY IN THE MORNING

cues.text: Riding in a way you can't help but double-click — and prove the magic still exists. Even here, it's chilly in the morning.
Fog covers the seas and hugs the tree-covered hills, floating through the morning as it exhales its introduction. This world is at peace.
In the awakening of dawn, in fresh muted colors: we can rebuild this temple. It's a new day — a catharsis for me to say, with newfound energies and recycled airs.
We can rebuild this temple — under vibrant sun rays of glory, of the wisdoms of morning dews and their winks of luck.
cues.screen: UNDER VIBRANT SUN RAYS OF GLORY

cues.text: With laps around infinity pools of edgeless dreams, that reflect the enormity of the skies.
cues.screen: EDGELESS DREAMS THAT REFLECT THE SKIES

cues.text: And of modern faiths — that we too can walk on water. Deep breaths, in appreciation of present life, and our present positions.
cues.screen: THAT WE TOO CAN WALK ON WATER

cues.text: We can rebuild this temple. It's a new day. A catharsis. We can welcome a new day.
cues.screen: WE CAN WELCOME A NEW DAY
IT'S A NEW DAY. A CATHARSIS.

cues.text: Decades later, there is less time for words, and more space for laughter — hugs with no reason, and loud voices, so our hearts can be overheard.
Less time for words. More space for laughter.
cues.screen: SO OUR HEARTS CAN BE OVERHEARD

cues.text: Reflecting on legacies, and creeds once told — of elders, now past.
And is this a one-time occasion? we ask. Or will we make time, in the sands of burning hourglasses?
Before our winds part ways — to a next lifetime. This is brotherhood.
Find me at the harbor, at the small tables, watching.
cues.screen: FIND ME AT THE HARBOR, WATCHING

cues.text: The couples orbit each other the way Jupiter keeps its moons — close, and counted.
The elders clutch their pearls and pray. Life has burned all my love stories — victory-less seasons.
cues.screen: LIFE HAS BURNED ALL MY LOVE STORIES

cues.text: So I harvest the flowers instead — scarlet poppies, purple blossoms — and they become my power.
Then, a distant window. She says: you'll see me. Capture the eyes. Refocus. Step back. Say hello.
Don't make me leave. I escaped here for a reason.
cues.screen: I ESCAPED HERE FOR A REASON
DON'T MAKE ME LEAVE. I ESCAPED HERE FOR A REASON.

cues.text: A hot minute. The haze gathers on the water — and everything I built here learns to be weather: the city, the temple, the harbor.
It takes me last, and from the ground up. I am reluctant — but I have been weather before.
All black again. But no walls this time.
A life flashes the way a reel does: the window, the tambourine, the field, the stars, the candle, the daisy, the ride, the temple, the hourglass.
cues.screen: A LIFE FLASHES THE WAY A REEL DOES

cues.text: Our dance together is a victory — two entwined muses, as it ends.
cues.screen: OUR DANCE TOGETHER IS A VICTORY

cues.text: An old door, from a vintage somewhere. It opens on a slow party — the kind I once fell out of a window to escape. This time, I choose the door.
cues.screen: THIS TIME, I CHOOSE THE DOOR
WHERE YOU GO WHEN YOU LEAVE - END OF PART 2: FUTURE

worlds.thesis: Recovery is not retrieval: the heart and the hands come back on their own terms, and the self's only work is to walk, kneel, and receive — nevermore said once per organ.
worlds.tone: Patient and solitary; small false glints delay the bodily restoration.

worlds.logline: A DJ is lowered into the house on a beam of light, the needle rings the room, and the poet — eyes wide shut, chin nested down — tells the whole love story over a rising fader: ghosts in vineyards, rings diverging, a home trucked apart, eleven petals plunked off a daisy, three roads and one silver lining — until the chin nests high and the volume clips.
worlds.thesis: Being heard is a gain structure: the same story at level one is grief and at level eight is testimony — the fader, not the words, is what turns forth to face delights and shadows.
worlds.tone: Exposed and insistent; the performance moves from lowered chin to claimed voice.

movements.label: CHIN NESTED
movements.line: DJ, turn me up, please. Eyes wide shut, chin nested at the arch of the weight of these spoken words.

movements.label: VINEYARD GHOSTS
movements.line: I have a love story to tell — of ghosts, whispering unfolded dilutions, birthed in purity, and dying in the vineyards of sun-soaked evergreen fields, unnourished.

movements.label: THOUSAND LIGHT YEARS
movements.line: One by one, treasures escaping — devaluing themselves after unsullied stars diminished their glares. I walked a thousand light years to be heard. So DJ — please — turn me up.

movements.label: DIVERGING RINGS
movements.line: So I can speak: of wedding bands diverging across abstract skies of wounded souls. Of a shared home, boxed and trucked on separate one-way streets — not built with U-turns, or stop, maybe-we-shouldn't signs.

movements.label: ELEVEN PETALS
movements.line: A love story of years — eleven years — each plunkled off as daisy petals. We love, we not. Of a future gone swiftly, and a past left empty-handed.

movements.label: THREE ROADS
movements.line: To pick a road: of heavy rain. Or of frontal fog. Or of dimmed night lights under a cloud — with a silver lining.

movements.label: CHIN HIGH
movements.line: Now, turning forth to face delights and shadows — one night at a time; one tear at a time; one open mic at a time. Chin now nested high, and volume turnt up.

worlds.title: NEWLY SINGLE
worlds.tagline: a soul leaves a body on a dance floor

motifs.two-clocks: the film's grammar: jitter vs. glide in the same frame
motifs.the-haze-grown-up: Film 01's vape returns as the smoke he chooses to breathe
motifs.the-withheld-ring: the suite's first gesture refused on purpose

characters.POET-BODY: two-tone until the split; then a single-shade husk on the fast clock, no bar, no pulse
characters.POET-SOUL: a thin outline of light on the slow clock, carrying both named stars
characters.ANGELS: two winged pourers on the slow clock, vessels tilted, streams converging on the husk
characters.THE RING: six segments; trembles on every fourth frame; never crosses the railing

worlds.logline: On a rooftop running faster than its own night, the poet's soul steps out of his body, watches all of Atlantis top-down, stands at the equator of a hotter planet, lets angels pour moon-salted ice baths over the husk he left dancing — then returns, leans back, breathes the whole room in, and at the railing holds a ring out over the edge and cannot let it go.
worlds.thesis: Separation is a frame-rate: the body grieves at the world's speed and the soul at its own — and what returns from the split is not relief but accuracy: what isn't mine, I still can not give.
worlds.tone: Restless bodily rhythm against the slower drift of the soul.

movements.label: PULSING
movements.line: Pulsing, and head throbbing from the music — and empty, on a crowded floor of sweated perfumes and temptations.

movements.label: THE ESCAPE
movements.line: The soul escapes my body, and leaves him on the dance floor — just flesh and bones. Rejection and heartache hit different, with no feelings afloat.

movements.label: IMAGINE MY BODY
movements.line: I want my soul to imagine my body. Watch strangers collide and spark electric currents that gamut the mood. We want him to be the last to leave.

movements.label: THE EQUATOR
movements.line: Now let us put my soul in the middle of an open field — at the equator of a planet much larger than my own, and much hotter.

movements.label: COOL ME DOWN
movements.line: Cool me down: pouring unfiltered water out of ice baths, salted from the closest moons, from angles of the newest religions — their graces curse or bless me. Only infinity will tell.

movements.label: BACK TO MY BODY
movements.line: Now bring my soul back to my body: to lean back, breathe in the smoke that fills the room — how good it is to finally get acquainted with the night.

movements.label: MOUNTAINS IN THE DISTANCE
movements.line: Unfamiliar, yet relatable mountains in the distance; wandering thoughts within reach. Accepting you'll never say, nor feel, my love was real. What isn't mine, I still can not give.

worlds.title: YET, HEARD

motifs.the-widening-gap: separation as a monotone function of film time
motifs.time-compression: moon phases, tree seasons, window generations around one steady walk
motifs.the-inset: the living room as a panel whose border collects the tears
motifs.the-borrowed-suitcase: what stays standing after the person is weather

characters.POET: two-tone, two orbit stars; reaches once through the crowd and once for the handlebars
characters.EX: back-turned in every appearance, as always; dissolves stroke by stroke, leaving a suitcase
characters.MOTHER: seated in an inset living room with a lamp and a prayer above her head
characters.FATHER: walks a half-step ahead; his footprints light when the son's feet find them
characters.THE PAIR: the background clock: gap 2 to 24 pixels across four beats

worlds.logline: Through a fawning crowd, past a moon that runs its phases over one walk, into a phone booth twice — mother's living room arriving as an inset with a tear down its crease, father's footprints lighting under his son's feet — while the break-up widens in the background of every shot, until the EX dissolves to weather and a motorcycle blinks its lamp at the man left standing.
worlds.thesis: Farewell is not an event but a background process: it runs at its own rate behind every call, every walk, every prayer — and being heard does not stop it; it only means someone watched it happen with you.
worlds.tone: Tender but unresolved; adjacent spaces hold grief without settling it.

movements.label: THE SHARED MOON
movements.line: Before I go, we look at the moon the way we used to see it. We talk for years, travel through time — we grow old together, I believe. Maybe we could have it all.

movements.label: TEARS, AN ABYSS
movements.line: Before I go, I call on my mother — in tears, speaking of an abyss she's never known. We talk for years, re-closet wounds, and re-explain my way of birth. Even after prayer: what isn't mine, I still can not give.

movements.label: HIS FOOTSTEPS, RETRACED
movements.line: Before I go, I call on my father — his calming demeanor summoned from the yonders. We walk for years, east toward the sunrises, retracing his footsteps — my tears falling in the wave shadows of the inner harbor.

movements.label: EAST, AT THE HARBOR
movements.line: We stroll, father and son, hearted and shaken. Someone borrowed, and someone blue — yet, broken. Yet, heard.

worlds.title: MAGIC RIDE
worlds.tagline: night replaced by morning, dot by dot

motifs.the-crossing: register as landscape: crossed, not flipped
motifs.stars-come-inside: the orbit radius decays to zero; the pulse doubles
motifs.the-borrowed-suitcase: strapped behind the seat all the way to the shore
motifs.the-breath: the only cold thing in a warm frame — 'even here'

characters.POET: rider profile, leaning forward; brow-bar; heart pulse 1px in the dark, 2px after the stars come inside
characters.THE MACHINE: hex wheels with rotating spokes, tank, lamp; blissful and oddly sensitive; carries the borrowed suitcase
characters.THE BYSTANDERS: three, each with a two-tick head twist and a doubleclick blink
characters.LONELINESS: an eight-blob weather system, shredded on contact with the noise

worlds.logline: Not looking for a ride, he rubs his aggressions into the steel anyway — and one ride carries the whole film from black to white: through streets where heads twist twice, past loneliness shredded by his own noise, under a settling moon, across a grey hour where the frames themselves trade registers, into a believable morning that is chilly, and back to the shore where everything broke — arriving this time, not washing up.
worlds.thesis: The magic still existing is not an event but a direction: darkness is crossed at riding speed, the stars you were given come inside, and the same shore means something different when you choose to stop there.
worlds.tone: Independent, quietly amused and increasingly open; night gives way to morning.

movements.label: HOP ON
movements.line: I wasn't looking for a ride, but here you are — blissful, and oddly sensitive. I rub my aggressions into your steel coverings, and hop on.

movements.label: HEADS TWIST
movements.line: Loneliness is having everything with no one to tell — being everywhere, with no one to love. I let the noise block the noise. The way I ride: eyes turn, heads twist — and prove the magic still exists.

movements.label: MOON SETTLES
movements.line: All preparations to live and dream in darkness, I no longer desire. The moon settles, and the tease of distant stars subsides — and I can see a morning ahead for me.

movements.label: NIGHT REPLACED
movements.line: It looks like a morning I could believe in — a morning where loss and life aren't so — well — ripe with sunlight that's deceptively warm. The chirping of birds, fueling of nests, spring out of the night that has covered me.

movements.label: BLISSFUL, INNOCENT
movements.line: With my own curiosities, for a chance at an end wherever everything will be OK. I want to live in this feeling forever — blissful, and oddly innocent.

movements.label: CHILLY MORNING
movements.line: Riding in a way you can't help but double-click — and prove the magic still exists. Even here, it's chilly in the morning.

worlds.title: NEW DAY
worlds.tagline: the temple assembles, one course at a time

motifs.recycled-airs: the ruin is the quarry; the arch is the door
motifs.edgeless: the pool's far edge never drawn — infinity by omission
motifs.walking-on-water: faith as a compositing trick the film commits to

characters.POET: white-register ink, pulse doubled to 2px since the stars came inside; walks on water at scale 0.62
characters.THE TEMPLE: an assembly parameter: platform 0.05, pillars 0.26, shell 0.34-0.62, inner sweep, needle 0.72, ramp 0.78, opening 0.85, fins 0.92
characters.THE STONES: five, recycled from Films 03-04's shore, each with a lift arc and a settle
characters.THE REFLECTION: the same function, mirrored about y=66, shades folded to 1-2, wobbling with the water

worlds.logline: The fog exhales its introduction over the ruin, and the ruin answers by lifting itself: stones float into a new base course, the broken arch straightens into a doorway, a parabolic shell draws itself left to right — and when the water arrives edgeless, the temple learns to reflect, the poet walks the waterline with his own inversion underfoot, and the sun ends up overhead.
worlds.thesis: Catharsis is construction with the original materials: nothing new arrives — the same stones, the same arch, the same man — only the schedule runs the other way.
worlds.tone: Calm reconstruction; masonry answers the earlier chapel damage.

movements.label: MORNING FOG
movements.line: Fog covers the seas and hugs the tree-covered hills, floating through the morning as it exhales its introduction. This world is at peace.

movements.label: FIRST COURSES
movements.line: In the awakening of dawn, in fresh muted colors: we can rebuild this temple. It's a new day — a catharsis for me to say, with newfound energies and recycled airs.

movements.label: COLUMNS AND BEAMS
movements.line: We can rebuild this temple — under vibrant sun rays of glory, of the wisdoms of morning dews and their winks of luck.

movements.label: THE INFINITY POOL
movements.line: With laps around infinity pools of edgeless dreams, that reflect the enormity of the skies.

movements.label: WALKING ON WATER
movements.line: And of modern faiths — that we too can walk on water. Deep breaths, in appreciation of present life, and our present positions.

movements.label: A NEW DAY
movements.line: We can rebuild this temple. It's a new day. A catharsis. We can welcome a new day.

worlds.title: REUNION
worlds.tagline: less time for words, more space for laughter

motifs.words-to-laughter: a probability crossfade as the film's grammar
motifs.the-sundial: the sun patch crossing the floor is the film's clock
motifs.the-flip: the poem's question answered by a hand, not a line

characters.POET: brow-bar and 2px pulse; hugs three times; last to remain, hand raised
characters.THE FRIENDS: three, single-tone, each with a pulse phase that surrenders on embrace
characters.THE ELDERS: Film 05's crowned figures, indoors, shade-2 faint, flickering at the edges of their stay
characters.THE HOURGLASS: burning grains with one-pixel flames; flipped at 0.55-0.68 of its beat

worlds.logline: Decades later, inside the temple they rebuilt, three friends arrive through a door of light, trade their words in for laughter, go quiet for the crowned elders who stand faintly among them, flip the burning hourglass rather than let the occasion be one-time — and part ways trailing curls of wind, hearts still blinking in unison.
worlds.thesis: Brotherhood is a shared clock: the hug synchronizes it, the laughter funds it, the flip extends it — and the winds can part ways without breaking the tempo.
worlds.tone: Warm familiarity; individual gestures become shared laughter.

movements.label: HUGS WITH NO REASON
movements.line: Decades later, there is less time for words, and more space for laughter — hugs with no reason, and loud voices, so our hearts can be overheard.

movements.label: LESS TIME, MORE SPACE
movements.line: Less time for words. More space for laughter.

movements.label: ELDERS, NOW PAST
movements.line: Reflecting on legacies, and creeds once told — of elders, now past.

movements.label: BURNING HOURGLASSES
movements.line: And is this a one-time occasion? we ask. Or will we make time, in the sands of burning hourglasses?

movements.label: WINDS PART
movements.line: Before our winds part ways — to a next lifetime. This is brotherhood.

worlds.title: HOW TO WIN MY HEART

motifs.orbital-watching: desire studied as mechanics before it is risked
motifs.char-eaten-pages: the burned stories kept, not discarded
motifs.the-focus-pull: attention drawn as rendering: two frames where only she is solid
motifs.the-staying: the suite's second refusal (after the withheld ring) — this one toward, not away

characters.POET: seated more than standing, for the first time in the suite; bouquet of eight; bold outline once the power is worn
characters.HOPE: a silhouette in one lit window across the water, facing out; never closer than distant
characters.THE ELDERS: two benches — one pair clutching pearls, one praying
characters.THE FLOWERS: poppies as dark rounds, blossoms as crossed dots; ten stalks, eight taken

worlds.logline: At the harbor cafe he watches couples orbit like Jupiter's moons and elders clutch what they kept, while his own love stories sit char-eaten at his elbow — so he harvests the flowers into his power instead, until a distant lit window says YOU'LL SEE ME, and instead of leaving toward anything, he sets the bouquet on the rail and sits back down: don't make me leave; I escaped here for a reason.
worlds.thesis: Winning this heart is not pursuit but placement: stay where you escaped to, put the gathered power somewhere visible, and let the window keep its light on.
worlds.tone: Watchful and guarded; attention gradually risks remaining with another person.

movements.label: SMALL TABLES
movements.line: Find me at the harbor, at the small tables, watching.

movements.label: COUNTED ORBITS
movements.line: The couples orbit each other the way Jupiter keeps its moons — close, and counted.

movements.label: BURNED STORIES
movements.line: The elders clutch their pearls and pray. Life has burned all my love stories — victory-less seasons.

movements.label: HARVESTED POWER
movements.line: So I harvest the flowers instead — scarlet poppies, purple blossoms — and they become my power.

movements.label: REFOCUS
movements.line: Then, a distant window. She says: you'll see me. Capture the eyes. Refocus. Step back. Say hello.

movements.label: WON'T LEAVE
movements.line: Don't make me leave. I escaped here for a reason.

worlds.title: HOT MINUTE
worlds.tagline: everything learns to be weather, then a door

motifs.fade-schedules: each built thing greys on its own clock; the flowers hold longest
motifs.the-suite-recalled: twelve memory panels: the films as their own B-roll

characters.POET: taken feet-first, pulse last; floats whole in the black; enters the door back-turned — the suite's final figure is himself, seen the way the EX always was
characters.THE HAZE: the suite's antagonist material completing its arc: vape, dissolution, smoke, weather, and finally the medium of passage
characters.THE MUSE: the thin light outline, entwined for one beat, never named
characters.THE DOOR: vintage, paneled, knob glinting; opens on warm silhouettes at half clock; closes to a line, then keeps what it took

worlds.logline: The haze gathers on the water and takes everything he built — boats, cafe, her window gently, the flowers last — then takes him ground-up until only the pulse blinks in the black. What follows is the suite remembering itself in twelve flashes, a dance of two entwined muses around one center, and an old vintage door opening on a slow warm party: the kind he once fell out of a window to escape, and now walks into, from the back, at his own speed, as the door closes and keeps him.
worlds.thesis: Leaving and arriving are the same door seen from different registers: the suite opens with a fall out of a window and closes with a walk through a door — and the victory is not escaping the party, but choosing it.
worlds.tone: Intense but accepting; built forms dissolve while remembered relations recur.

movements.label: EVERYTHING I BUILT
movements.line: A hot minute. The haze gathers on the water — and everything I built here learns to be weather: the city, the temple, the harbor.

movements.label: FROM THE GROUND UP
movements.line: It takes me last, and from the ground up. I am reluctant — but I have been weather before.

movements.label: NO WALLS
movements.line: All black again. But no walls this time.

movements.label: THE REEL
movements.line: A life flashes the way a reel does: the window, the tambourine, the field, the stars, the candle, the daisy, the ride, the temple, the hourglass.

movements.label: TWO ENTWINED MUSES
movements.line: Our dance together is a victory — two entwined muses, as it ends.

movements.label: I CHOOSE THE DOOR
movements.line: An old door, from a vintage somewhere. It opens on a slow party — the kind I once fell out of a window to escape. This time, I choose the door.

1.name: Solid perception
1.difference: One body owns the frame: either we see through its eyes (POV, eyelid/mask/windscreen framing) or we see it held at the hub with everything else arranged around it — and the image would lose its organising centre if that body were removed.

family.title: Indisch allerlei
family.note: Binocular mask: a distant ship held as the object of one gaze.

family.title: The House I Live In
family.note: Rifle-scope crosshair: the world arrives already centred on one eye.

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 4) (Part I)
family.note: Peephole vignette: the frame becomes a single perceiver's aperture.

family.title: 6 1/2 Magic Hours
family.note: Through the windscreen: the road is organised around the driver's seat.

family.title: Winter in Den haag / IJs in Den Haag
family.note: Looking down at one's own skates: the perceiver's body enters its own view.

family.title: Eyes and Their Care (An Introduction), The
family.note: Eyes looking into the lens: the reverse shot that names the perceiving centre.

2.name: Liquid perception
2.difference: The centre moves: in a continuous reframing the shot passes from one character or environment to another, each central only until the next captures the screen.

family.title: Straight Talk
family.note: Following walkers into a crowd: perception passes from body to body.

family.title: Episode 19 - The Soil Explorers
family.note: Water-level view of a wake: vision carried on liquid movement.

family.title: A Poem in Marble, A Place on the Map: Byron R. White U.S. Courthouse, Denver, CO
family.note: Corridor tracking shot: the centre travels, handed from space to space.

family.title: The National Wildlife Refuges of Alaska
family.note: A boat drifting midstream: the camera floats with the current, not a subject.

family.title: Master Hands (Part IV)
family.note: Drifting over a factory floor: the view slides across many workers' stations.

family.title: The Fed Today
family.note: A street crowd flowing past the lens: no one holds the frame for long.

3.name: Gaseous perception
3.difference: Nothing is privileged: through slow/fast motion, superimposition, fragmentation or micro-shooting the image treats a human figure as one image like any other among landscapes, matter and machines.

family.title: Photography
family.note: Microscopy: matter seen from no human scale.

family.title: Fitting Faces
family.note: A field of lenses or bubbles: each image varies with every other.

family.title: Water
family.note: Light breaking on water: an acentred field of flickers.

family.title: Fashion's Favorite (Part I)
family.note: A macro lattice of fibres: pattern without a subject.

family.title: Amateur Film Medicus09a
family.note: Surf on a shore: waves acting on one another with no one watching.

family.title: Telephone and Telegraph
family.note: Banks of relays: the machine registers signals with no operator.

4.name: Icon
4.difference: The face is not a feature of a person in a space but the whole image: a close-up in which expression (fixed wonder or traversing micro-movements) holds an intensity that has not yet become action.

family.title: Story of Television
family.note: Eyes shut, cheek lit: a face turned inward, an icon of quality.

family.title: Place to Live, A
family.note: A boy's face fills the frame: wonder held before any action.

family.title: Eyes and Their Care (An Introduction), The
family.note: An upturned child's face in tight close-up: the face as reflecting surface.

family.title: Coney Island - Food (Standard 4:3)
family.note: A woman's face half in shadow: expression with no motor outlet.

family.title: THE PHOTOGRAPHER
family.note: A weathered old face: a lifetime of qualities written as surface.

family.title: Episode 10 - The EFNEP Program
family.note: A woman's pained face: a power rising (icon of power).

5.name: Dividual
5.difference: The feeling belongs to the gathering: the crowd, pack or series of faces is individualised as one affect while each person in it is de-individualised.

family.title: Coney Island
family.note: A packed beach crowd: a mass in which faces stay legible.

family.title: Unique Contribution, The (Part II)
family.note: A flock moving as one body, each animal still distinct.

family.title: Space Ship Takeoff, a Technical Fantasy
family.note: An audience facing one screen: one affect spread across the seats.

family.title: Look to Lockheed for Leadership (Part I)
family.note: A shift crowd streaming through the gates: individual gaits inside one flow.

family.title: Winter in Den haag / IJs in Den Haag
family.note: Onlookers huddled in winter: a collective stance.

family.title: Bosque del Apache National Wildlife Refuge
family.note: Birds lifting together: one gesture made by thousands.

6.name: Any-space-whatever
6.difference: Affect with no face: an emptied, disconnected or amorphous space (fog, rain, shadow, coloured void, ruin, haze) that expresses a quality itself rather than locating an action.

family.title: Old Time Tractor Plowing Dry Land
family.note: A field in fog: space as pure grey potential.

family.title: Dust Storm
family.note: A dust storm whites out the land: space without coordinates.

family.title: Shock Troops of Disaster: The Story of the New England Hurricane
family.note: Dark water in a flooded street at night: geography turned amorphous.

family.title: American Road, The (Part III)
family.note: A sun flare swallows the road: light dissolves the place.

family.title: San Francisco Earthquake Aftermath, Part 1
family.note: Earthquake rubble, no one in sight: a disconnected space.

family.title: Berlin: Symphony of a Great City
family.note: An empty station under a canopy: a transit space emptied of use.

7.name: Symptom
7.difference: The body acts from a drive too strong for it: a visible primordial act (devouring, rutting, seizing, cruelty) in which the human behaves as a human animal, not as an agent with a goal.

family.title: The National Wildlife Refuges of Alaska
family.note: An animal tearing at raw meat: drive with no mediation, the impulse too strong for the body.

family.title: Nature's Cameo: Bryce Canyon National Park
family.note: Animals fighting in snow: primal force breaking through the milieu.

family.title: Valley Town
family.note: A hunched man eating: need takes over posture.

family.title: Robinson Crusoe B
family.note: A fur-clad castaway: a body returned to the animal.

family.title: Inside the Fed
family.note: Hands grabbing across a counter: appetite in the gesture.

family.title: Best Food In Town
family.note: Food taken from the plate: the partial object of hunger.

8.name: Fetish
8.difference: A partial object is held apart and charged — relic or vult — so that the image makes us feel stored primal force in it, waiting for a body to discharge it.

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 4) (Part I)
family.note: A carved figure lit alone: an object holding primal power.

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 5) (Part I)
family.note: An object glowing red in the dark: stored energy.

family.title: Speech: Platform Posture and Appearance
family.note: A pair of shoes isolated at floor level: Deamer's list includes the shoe.

family.title: Verkade's fabrieken te Zaandam
family.note: A hand turning a small object under a lamp: the partial object handled.

family.title: Laboratory Design for Microbiological Safety
family.note: An empty glass display case: the reliquary awaiting its charge.

9.name: Originary world
9.difference: Beneath a recognisable place rumbles an archetypal one: the forest, desert, swamp or house is shown as a determinate but timeless ground of drives and decay, not as a historical setting.

family.title: Watershed wildfire
family.note: Wildfire at night: raw element devouring the milieu.

family.title: Airport America
family.note: A drowned dead forest: a swamp of pre-human force.

family.title: [Amateur film: "Frisco Fair / Pacific Northwest"]
family.note: A dark forest shot through with light: the forest world of Innocence.

family.title: General Health Habits
family.note: An isolated house under a black tree: the milieu gone primal.

family.title: Indië-materiaal van Willy Mullens
family.note: Figures on a jungle path: the forest swallowing a human procession.

family.title: [Completion of Northwestern Pacific Rail Road] (Part I)
family.note: A tunnel mouth in raw rock: the depths of the world opening.

10.name: Index of lack
10.difference: Something is visibly missing from the situation (an ellipsis) and the character's action fills it in one unequivocal disclosure that then redirects what they do.

family.title: Dating: Do's and Don'ts
family.note: A man at the door: the arrival implies a situation off-screen.

family.title: All My Babies
family.note: An examination at a bedside: a look that infers what happened.

family.title: Wreckless
family.note: A man entering a room: the door opens onto the missing situation.

family.title: Victory Gardens
family.note: Hands digging into soil: an action unearths what was hidden.

family.title: The Money Story
family.note: A hand uncovering a shape in sand: the situation disclosed by a gesture.

family.title: Space Shuttle: A Remarkable Flying Machine
family.note: A circle of light in the dark: searching makes the scene appear.

11.name: Index of equivocity
11.difference: An action discloses a situation that stays double: a slight difference in the same act refers it to two distant situations at once — 'this and that' — and the film sustains the undecidability.

family.title: All My Babies
family.note: An embrace that reads as comfort or as restraint.

family.title: Key to Our Horizons
family.note: A hand at a lock: entering, or breaking in?

family.title: Fighter for Freedom: The Frederick Douglass Story
family.note: A man lifting a child: rescue or seizure.

family.title: The Electric House
family.note: Two identical doors: two worlds behind one gesture.

family.title: The Playhouse
family.note: A figure in a dark doorway: welcome or threat.

12.name: Vector
12.difference: Many characters each disclose a partial, equivocal situation, and only their interlocking over the film draws the broken, unpredictable but necessary line of one world.

family.title: Formations
family.note: Cars crossing an intersection from above: separate trajectories in one space.

family.title: Scatter radar: Space research from the ground
family.note: A street market from above: each figure on its own errand.

family.title: Broadway Limited
family.note: Tracks braiding and splitting: the broken line whose path is unpredictable.

family.title: Restaurant Operator, The
family.note: Cooks at separate stations: Ajami's interlocking, unrelated tasks.

family.title: Ant City
family.note: Ants each on its own route: many partial situations in one field.

family.title: Trading Centers of the Pacific Coast
family.note: Trails crossing and recrossing: the record of many unfinished journeys.

13.name: Milieu
13.difference: The situation is given before anyone acts: an establishing or extreme wide shot lays out a determined geo-historical and social space, and the people in it exemplify it rather than change it.

family.title: Mechanical Engineering at duPont
family.note: An industrial town from above: the determinate world that will call for action.

family.title: Nature's Cameo: Bryce Canyon National Park
family.note: Cowboys driving cattle across open range: the western milieu and its tasks.

family.title: How Our Country Grew
family.note: A dense town seen from the air: the milieu as an encompassing whole.

family.title: This Is My Railroad (Part I)
family.note: A rail yard and signal tower: a world of working functions.

family.title: Letter From an Airline Pilot (Part I)
family.note: A lecturer before a classroom diagram: the social order explained, as in marxism today's GDR classroom.

family.title: Boulder Dam
family.note: Desert with yucca: the geography that shapes whoever enters it.

14.name: Binomial
14.difference: Two opposed lines of force, embodied in characters, face each other: the image is organised as a duel (violent, romantic, political) pointing toward a decisive confrontation.

family.title: [Amateur films: Ivan Besse collection: Britton, South Dakota 1938-39] (Part VII)
family.note: Two teams at the line of scrimmage: the world polarised into sides.

family.title: Cabeza Prieta National Wildlife Refuge Desert Wilderness
family.note: Two rams squaring off on a ridge: the duel in nature.

family.title: Working Together: A Case History in Labor-Management Cooperation
family.note: Labour and management face to face: the duel of Made in Dagenham.

family.title: We Learn About the Telephone I
family.note: Two cartoon figures eye to eye: the binomial as pure form.

family.title: De graal pinksterzegen
family.note: Two rows of figures facing each other: a ceremony of opposition.

15.name: Imprint
15.difference: A complex situation has entered one body: the character carries it as visible, contained pressure, often fixed on an emotional object that links them to the world, before (or as) it bursts into action.

family.title: Twenty-Four Hours of Progress (Part II)
family.note: A hard-hatted worker, head bowed: labour written into the body.

family.title: De Joodsche invalide
family.note: A bedridden woman holding a keepsake: the world pressed into an object.

family.title: Going Steady?
family.note: A young man brooding: the situation turned inward.

family.title: Ole' 23
family.note: A boy looking out at the school bus: the environment weighing on a small figure.

family.title: FIVE ARTISTS
family.note: A lone figure before a monumental facade: the building's order bearing down.

family.title: Consumers Want to Know (Part I)
family.note: A man by a turntable: like Fish Tank's record, the world held in a charged object.

16.name: Plastic figure
16.difference: Does a single on-screen object, action or cut stand in, in one stroke, for a real situation that is never itself shown (metaphor/metonymy/synecdoche), while the film's own drive is still action discovering situation?

family.title: Western Cattle Sequence
family.note: Cattle in the slaughter pens: the abattoir as trope for a massacre.

family.title: [Chevrolet Sales Convention Musical]
family.note: A showroom song-and-dance number: spectacle swallows the everyday, as in The Wandering Cloud.

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 4) (Part III)
family.note: A line of posed bathing beauties: a staged spectacle wrapping an implied desire.

family.title: Coffee Break
family.note: An hourglass: a small object made to stand for a whole situation of time.

family.title: National Wildlife Refuge System
family.note: A wildlife stamp: a miniature standing in for a whole landscape.

17.name: Theatrical figure
17.difference: Is a fictitious action (performance, game, allegory, parody) being played out over a sequence as a precursor of a real action that has not yet happened and keeps being deferred?

family.title: [San Francisco General Strike] (Part II)
family.note: A staged first-aid drill: rehearsing the real emergency.

family.title: Sleep for Health
family.note: Two boys sparring: the fight rehearsed as play.

family.title: The Snow Queen (Animation)
family.note: A cartoon battle: conflict rehearsed in animation, as in Scott Pilgrim.

family.title: Where the Sun Reigns
family.note: A massed drill: war performed before it is fought.

family.title: Powers Music School Presents: Musical Story Hour 02/28/09
family.note: A school stage show under a skull banner: fiction dressing a threat.

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 5) (Part I)
family.note: A puppet stage: a fictive action that prefigures the real.

18.name: Mise en abyme
18.difference: Do figures nest inside figures such that, watching, you cannot say whether a performed sequence contains an emblematic image or an emblematic image contains the performed sequence?

family.title: Television Remote Control (Tuner)
family.note: A woman watching a television that shows another scene: an image within the image.

family.title: THE PHOTOGRAPHER
family.note: A photographer at his tripod: the film showing a picture being made.

family.title: Fastax-tion
family.note: A cameraman filming from a rig: the apparatus inside its own picture.

family.title: 1959 RCA 21-inch TV Screen
family.note: A television set mid-broadcast: the screen doubled inside the screen.

family.title: Let's Go To The Movies
family.note: An audience at the movies: cinema watching itself.

19.name: Figure of the sublime
19.difference: Does the character's action visibly exceed anything the situation requires, so that the grandiose act makes the situation look futile (a steamship hauled over a mountain)?

family.title: The Balloonatic
family.note: Keaton's The Balloonatic: a visionary contraption, doomed.

family.title: American Road, The (Part I)
family.note: A land yacht sailing the highway: the grand gesture exceeds the road.

family.title: Amateur Film - Little Journeys to Niagara
family.note: A giant wheeled contraption: the crazy enterprise built in hardware.

family.title: The Battling Kangaroo
family.note: A boxing kangaroo: a spectacle out of all proportion to its occasion.

family.title: Belo Horizonte
family.note: Earthworks carving a hillside: action bigger than the world asked for.

family.title: Auto-Lite on Parade
family.note: A massed parade in formation: spectacle swollen beyond its purpose.

20.name: Figure of enfeeblement
20.difference: Do a weak character's small, futile acts make an immense, indifferent world swell into view (the tiny point fleeing to the horizon), rather than the world merely sitting there?

family.title: Aqua Frolics
family.note: A small boat tossed in surf: the power belongs to the sea.

family.title: Oil Across Arabia
family.note: A figure in the Arabian desert: the landscape outscales every act.

family.title: Amateur Film Children Playing Near Hudson
family.note: A man sitting idle in a garden chair: Slackistan's drift.

family.title: San Francisco Earthquake Aftermath, Part 1
family.note: People dwarfed by a ruined city: the disaster discloses the world's scale.

family.title: Heavenly Bodies
family.note: A small figure on an empty path: going nowhere across the frame.

family.title: AUTOMOBILE ECONOMY TEST, ca. 1938
family.note: An empty sea horizon: the world vast, the actor almost absent.

21.name: Quotidian
21.difference: Is an everyday act shown so that you cannot decide whether it is trivial or heroic, the situation both inconsequential and unfathomable at once?

family.title: Health: Your Posture
family.note: A woman at household chores: repetition, sublime and futile.

family.title: Inside/Outside: The Story of Food and Fitness
family.note: A couple eating at the kitchen table: the meal as a whole life.

family.title: Industry on Parade: Sylacauga Saga
family.note: A swimmer diving into a pool: A Screaming Man's pool, the everyday made grave.

family.title: Century of Progress Exposition: Wings of a Century
family.note: A high dive against an empty sky: heroic and trivial in one movement.

family.title: Story of a City: New York
family.note: Washing on a line: the most ordinary thing, patiently held.

family.title: Door to Heaven, The
family.note: A curtained room with a lamp: domestic space where nothing happens.

22.name: Limit of the large form action-image
22.difference: Before acting, does the character have to extract a question hidden in the situation (what is a samurai now?), so action is delayed into a considered response rather than an explosive reaction?

family.title: Nieuwe stormramp in den Achterhoek
family.note: A house wrecked by flood: the situation no longer calls for action; it poses a question.

family.title: Indië-materiaal van Willy Mullens
family.note: A column of people moving through jungle: an evacuation with no visible enemy.

family.title: Colaci Home Movies: Family 1952-1956 (Part I)
family.note: An adobe wall in empty desert: like the wall in Monsters, a boundary whose meaning is unclear.

family.title: Indisch allerlei
family.note: A ruined wall overgrown by jungle: the hidden problem inside the milieu.

family.title: Airport America
family.note: A low plane over farmland: threat or routine?

23.name: Limit of the small form action-image
23.difference: Do parallel, heterogeneous lines of action connect only as pieces from different puzzles, so the situation they reveal remains an unanswered cipher, a sustained ellipsis?

family.title: Apollo 12: Pinpoint for Science
family.note: Hands fitting map pieces together: fragments that never close into a whole.

family.title: Principles of Electricity
family.note: Letter blocks scattered on a table: the clues stay heterogeneous.

family.title: Arteries of New York City
family.note: Tenement fronts: like the projects in Brooklyn's Finest, a situation read in pieces.

family.title: [Amateur film: Wathen collection: Greenwich Village, New York Snowstorm, and Coney Island]
family.note: Two men in suits on a tenement street: plain-clothes watch, meaning withheld.

family.title: Third Avenue El
family.note: The street seen from the elevated railway: partial evidence from above.

24.name: Limit of the action-image (extreme limit)
24.difference: Is the film permeated by problems from start to end so that you can no longer tell whether they are posed by the situation or discovered by action, the world itself appearing as a field of indeterminate forces?

family.title: Where the Bankers Bank
family.note: An armoured truck and its guard: Metro Manila's van, the job that has itself become the problem.

family.title: Logic By Machine (Part II)
family.note: A man in profile beside a logic machine: thinking takes the place of acting.

family.title: Boulder Dam
family.note: A black hole blasted in rock: a cipher at the centre of the world.

family.title: Men, Steel and Earthquakes
family.note: Workers amid excavation rubble: a world of problems no single act resolves.

25.name: Rich dream
25.difference: Is the passage into the dream explicitly marked and ornately made (dissolves, superimpositions, effects), with an equally marked exit, so the dream is attributed to a dreamer and recognised as dream by the viewer?

family.title: Man of Action
family.note: A cartoon thought-cloud: the dream bubble, clearly bracketed off from waking.

family.title: Fastax-tion
family.note: A distorted, stretched close-up: the image bends into dream.

family.title: What's It to You? (Part I)
family.note: A kaleidoscope: an optical sign announcing that we have entered another regime.

family.title: How the Ear Functions
family.note: Glowing spheres floating in black: a dream space set clearly apart.

family.title: [Amateur films: Ivan Besse collection: Britton, South Dakota 1938-39] (Part V)
family.note: A smear of blurred motion: the device that marks the passage into dream.

26.name: Restrained dream
26.difference: Is the dream entered by an invisible cut and made of concrete everyday things with one impossible unhinging, so that the film's task becomes deciding whether we are awake?

family.title: Programmer with Magic Memory: Another Newsmaker
family.note: A man dozing in an armchair: we can't tell when sleep began.

family.title: POTTERY, ca. 1926
family.note: A cup blurred at the edge of focus: the everyday slightly off.

family.title: Let Yourself Go
family.note: A woman opening a door onto darkness: an unmarked passage between worlds.

family.title: Fastax-tion
family.note: A hand with a cigarette against black: an isolated detail oddly insisted upon.

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 4) (Part II)
family.note: A dim window onto a blank wall: realism gone uncanny.

family.title: Master Hands
family.note: A gaunt worker at a machine in low light: the lathe of The Machinist, waking life already dreamlike.

27.name: Movement of world
27.difference: Is there no entry or exit at all: does the world itself carry the character along (song, dance, impossible events treated as natural) so that no one is the dreamer?

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 1) (Part I)
family.note: A chorus line on a lit stage: the musical where the décor dances, Deleuze's movement of world.

family.title: The Snow Queen (Animation)
family.note: A lantern floating through an animated night: a dream with no dreamer to wake.

family.title: Coney Island At Night (Standard 4:3)
family.note: Coney Island rides at night: the world itself spinning in light.

family.title: Drive-in Intermission 6
family.note: An animated swirl: the setting animates itself.

family.title: Berlin: Symphony of a Great City
family.note: Berlin's city machine in motion: the world moves with dream logic.

family.title: Changing City, The
family.note: Skyscrapers slanting overhead: the city folding, as in Inception's Paris.

28.name: Strong destiny
28.difference: Does a marked flashback (pause, dissolve, monochrome, reverb) return to the present and pass through affect into an action it determines, closing a causal circuit?

family.title: Mirror of America
family.note: A bleached, overexposed march: the past visibly marked as past.

family.title: Farmer Miller Goes Into High Gear (Part II)
family.note: Hands holding old photographs: the recollection that will decide what happens.

family.title: Financial Investigation - Fundamentals
family.note: An older man in an armchair, lost in reverie: the moment before the flashback.

family.title: Singing Wires
family.note: A figure at a desk in lamplight: like the writer at the typewriter in The Secret in Their Eyes, the past pulling on the present.

family.title: Alcohol and the Human Body
family.note: A man lying back, eyes closed: memory about to take command.

29.name: Weak destiny
29.difference: Is the flashback ambiguous, incomplete or shared, so it saturates present feeling as a clue to an ellipsis that must be reconstructed before any action can follow?

family.title: NEW ORLEANS, ca. 1923
family.note: An old, worn street scene: a fragment of the past that belongs to no one.

family.title: Indië-materiaal van Willy Mullens
family.note: A colonial house and its veranda: a history hanging over the present without explaining it.

family.title: Cabeza Prieta National Wildlife Refuge Desert Wilderness
family.note: A lone figure on a dirt road through dry land: Maria's road in White Material, the past colouring every step.

family.title: Plant Solutions Video - Mini
family.note: Figures walking through tall grass: transit through a landscape charged with the past.

family.title: Golden Gate City
family.note: A crowded streetcar: bodies in transit, carrying histories no flashback explains.

family.title: Singing Wheels
family.note: A truck on a tree-lined road: movement suspended, destination uncertain.

30.name: Forking paths
30.difference: Do flashbacks fork within flashbacks, irreconcilably, so the past is explored for its own sake as an inexplicable secret and psychological causality is shown to be a ruse?

family.title: Going Steady?
family.note: A boy and his image in a hand mirror: the self doubled, each image an alternative.

family.title: Allegheny Portage Railroad
family.note: Tracks forking at a station: paths literally branching.

family.title: Back-Room Boy
family.note: A boat half-lost in fog: which crossing is this?

family.title: Health: Your Posture
family.note: Two faces mirroring each other: the double within one frame.

family.title: Small Steps...Giant Strides
family.note: A lone figure on a beach at dusk: Triangle's shore, where the loop restarts.

family.title: Oil Across Arabia
family.note: A ship alone at sea: Triangle's liner, the same voyage coming round again.

31.name: Mark
31.difference: Can you point to at least three occurrences of the same image or motif that the characters or viewer come to read as one habitual series with a meaning to be deciphered?

family.title: Place to Live, A
family.note: Identical row houses: repetition makes the relation visible.

family.title: According to Plan: The Story of Modern Sidewalls for the Homes of America
family.note: A planned street of matching houses: a pattern the viewer learns.

family.title: Big Train, The (Part I)
family.note: Glowing bulbs in a row: a series whose term is the single unit.

family.title: White Ammunition
family.note: Rows of cartridges: the series as a habit of the eye.

family.title: Communications Primer, A
family.note: A printed list: Se7en's lists, the series written down.

family.title: Two Pay Days (Part I)
family.note: A clerk at his ledger: the habitual entry, one more in the series.

32.name: Demark
32.difference: Does the shot show a known term of an established series appearing out of place or contradicting that series, so that the aberration itself shocks thought?

family.title: Finding Your Life's Work
family.note: Rows of identical figures with one singled out: the aberration drawn as a diagram.

family.title: Crop Duster
family.note: A crop-duster low over a field: Deleuze's demark, a plane dusting where there are no crops (North by Northwest).

family.title: Henry Ford's Mirror of America (Part II)
family.note: A line of marchers with one figure out of place.

family.title: Amateur Film Northwest
family.note: A flock with a stray: the series shows its rule by breaking it.

family.title: Miss Clark Introduces Panorama
family.note: A windmill: Hitchcock's mill turning against the wind, the natural series broken (Foreign Correspondent).

family.title: Insects
family.note: A creature coiled where it should not be: the snake in Buried's coffin.

33.name: Symbol
33.difference: Is a single concrete object held on screen as the knot where several separate threads of the film's relations meet, so that it carries an idea, belief or concept rather than a use or a desire?

family.title: Learning to Set Type
family.note: A lighter held in the dark: Buried's flame, an object carrying the film's ideas.

family.title: Industries of the United States: Steel - The Hardest Metal in the World
family.note: A padlock and chain: bondage as an idea you can hold.

family.title: 6 1/2 Magic Hours
family.note: A packed suitcase: departure thought through a thing.

family.title: Bookkeeping and You
family.note: A wristwatch in close-up: time as an object.

family.title: Key to Our Horizons
family.note: A hand turning a key: Hitchcock's key, a relation made into an object.

family.title: Let's Go To The Movies
family.note: A gramophone horn: voice and memory cast in brass.

34a.name: Opsign
34a.difference: With the sound off, is the image something to be seen and nothing more: no one's goal organises it, what moves in it resolves nothing, and the look is not converted into action?

family.title: Alice In Wonderland
family.note: A figure small on a sepia beach: Five's shoreline, a purely optical situation.

family.title: Alaska's Silver Millions (Part I)
family.note: A lone figure on a snowfield: action has stalled into looking.

family.title: Panama by Air (Reel 4)
family.note: Haze over the sea: a seeing that has nowhere to go.

family.title: Legacy for Wings
family.note: An old man looking out over wetland: the seer who no longer acts.

family.title: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge
family.note: A still marsh: duration with nothing to do.

family.title: Autoraces op boulevard Scheveningen
family.note: A seaside promenade with walkers crossing: Five's jetty, events without a plot.

34b.name: Sonsign
34b.difference: With the image covered, does a sound hold the scene as a situation in itself, not score, not plot-driving dialogue, not a cue someone answers?

family.title: Valley Town
family.note: A factory whistle on the roofline: the sound is the situation, and no worker is shown answering it. Audio analysis (heuristic): sound: low tonal hum, no speech.

family.title: Command Performance
family.note: A record turning on a phonograph in an empty room: sound on its own. Audio analysis (heuristic): sound, no speech rhythm.

family.title: Uruguay
family.note: People in a square beneath a loudspeaker pole: a sound situation no one answers. Audio analysis (heuristic): sound, steady, no speech rhythm.

family.title: Muscatatuck National Wildlife Refuge
family.note: A pond at dusk, frogs and birds: Five's toads, sound without an action attached. Audio analysis (heuristic): tonal: likely music score.

family.title: Communications and Our Town
family.note: A church belfry: bells heard over a town with no one moving. Audio analysis (heuristic): speech: likely narration.

family.title: Party Magic (Beich Screen Ad--"Whiz" Bar)
family.note: A family gathered still around the radio: hearing replaces doing. Audio analysis (heuristic): speech: likely narration.

35.name: Mirrors face to face
35.difference: Does one body or thing appear in the same shot as several reflections or doubles at once (facing, angled or distorting mirrors, glass), so that actual and virtual can no longer be told apart?

family.title: Frigidaire Finale 1957
family.note: A woman at her mirror: the actual image and its virtual double, face to face.

family.title: Day At The Fair, A
family.note: A funhouse distortion: the image multiplied and warped.

family.title: Barbers
family.note: A boy in the barber's mirror: the reflection returns the scene from another side.

family.title: De Joodsche invalide
family.note: A man beside his reflection: two images, neither simply first, as in Black Swan's mirrors.

family.title: Alchemist In Hollywood, The (Part II)
family.note: A strip of repeated frames: duplicates with no original.

family.title: Small Steps...Giant Strides
family.note: A faceted reflecting structure: fragments of one world across many planes.

36.name: Limpid and opaque
36.difference: During the shot or scene, does one face of the image clear (becomes visible or real) while the other clouds (becomes obscure or virtual), so that the two sides keep changing places?

family.title: Industry on Parade: Outgoing Cargo, Workhorses of the Harbor, Refresher Course
family.note: A figure behind a translucent screen: seen and unseen at once.

family.title: Under Western Stars
family.note: Figures before a projected image: the real and its image changing sides.

family.title: [Amateur film: Medicus collection: New York World's Fair, 1939-40] (Reel 3) (Part II)
family.note: A small stage, curtain parted: actor and role trading places, as in Self Made's workshop.

family.title: Mastering Takeoffs and Landings
family.note: A face lit by a blue screen: the actual lit by the virtual.

family.title: Dust Storm
family.note: A dust-hazed horizon: the visible sinking into the opaque.

37.name: Seed and environment
37.difference: Is there a small enclosed image (a snow globe, model, miniature stage, a drop, a crystal) that contains in germ the world that surrounds it or will grow from it, with seed and environment reversible?

family.title: Door to Heaven, The
family.note: A crystal cluster: the seed-crystal that could crystallise a whole environment.

family.title: Have I Told You Lately That I Love You?
family.note: A miniature monument: a model world, like the city in a warehouse in Synecdoche, New York.

family.title: Plant Solutions Video - Short
family.note: A sprouting seedling: a future environment folded into a seed.

family.title: New World Through Chemistry
family.note: A glass model: a virtual world held in a small transparent thing.

family.title: Unique Contribution, The (Part II)
family.note: A single red shoot: the germ before the milieu.

family.title: Wallops Island launch facility
family.note: A scale-model rocket: the seed of an environment still to be built.

38.name: Peaks of the present
38.difference: Does the narration give several different presents at once (a present of the past, a present of the present, a present of the future) in the same event, without flashback framing to rank them?

family.title: [First Private Atom Power Plant Opens]
family.note: A wall of clocks, each set to a different time: presents side by side.

family.title: Finale
family.note: Tilted screens with different images: several nows at once.

family.title: Introduction to Firearms
family.note: A blurred, ghostly figure: an impossible presence in the present, like Boonmee's ghost.

family.title: Man and Space
family.note: Dials on a control panel: parallel times read at a glance.

family.title: [Amateur film: Wathen collection: Greenwich Village, New York Snowstorm, and Coney Island]
family.note: A framed picture on an easel: another present hung inside this one.

family.title: Hotel and Restaurant Workers
family.note: A laid dining table: Boonmee's dinner, where the dead sit down with the living.

39.name: Sheets of the past
39.difference: Does the film move between regions of the past that coexist and ricochet non-chronologically (layered periods in one space, without a present-day narrator motivating each return)?

family.title: Miss Clark Introduces Panorama
family.note: A gallery of statues: pasts standing side by side.

family.title: Court to Court (Jun 2001)
family.note: A long arched corridor: a track through coexisting sheets of the past.

family.title: This is Russia (Reel 2 of 2)
family.note: A palace interior: Russian Ark's Hermitage, rooms as layers of time.

family.title: Justice Depends on You: Working for the Federal Courts
family.note: A vaulted hall: architecture holding centuries at once.

family.title: San Francisco Earthquake Aftermath, Part 6
family.note: Ruins after the earthquake: a stratum laid bare.

family.title: De Joodsche invalide
family.note: Dancers in white: Russian Ark's last ball, a sheet of the past still turning.

40.name: Powers of the false
40.difference: Does the film expose its own claim to truth, with testimony, performance or versions that pass into one another so that no image can be held as the true one?

family.title: How Our Country Grew
family.note: Rows of identical model houses: serialism, the copy without an original.

family.title: Thanksgiving Cooking Class 11/20/20
family.note: A woman speaking straight to camera: 24 City's testimony, where witness and actor can't be told apart.

family.title: From Trees to Tribunes (Part III)
family.note: Rows of identical workstations: 24 City's factory, repeated until it loses its ground.

family.title: RCA Presentation: Television, An
family.note: An audience in 3-D glasses: a crowd agreeing to a falsification.

family.title: The Mission of Apollo / Soyuz, ca. 1975
family.note: A man talking to the lens at work: a witness whose truth is a performance.

41.name: Bodies of attitude
41.difference: Is the body shown waiting, tired, slumped or posing, in its everydayness, with the posture itself as the content and no act prepared or completed?

family.title: Financial Investigation - Fundamentals
family.note: A man slumped back in his chair: the body's fatigue before any act.

family.title: Alcohol and the Human Body
family.note: A man asleep in an armchair: the everyday body, all attitude.

family.title: Back of the Mike
family.note: A man sitting alone on rocks: waiting that isn't going anywhere.

family.title: Out West
family.note: A figure lying on a boxcar: the drifting rider of I'm Not There.

family.title: Japan
family.note: A body curled in rest: posture as thought.

family.title: Toute La Bande, Episode 9: Bricolage
family.note: A woman repeating a kitchen chore: habit inscribed in the body.

42.name: Bodies of gest
42.difference: Are postures chained into a visible, repeated or staged gesture that performs a social act (ritual, bureaucratic routine, demonstration) and is shown as performance, not as efficient action?

family.title: The Mission of Apollo / Soyuz, ca. 1975
family.note: Dignitaries in a row: posture as rank.

family.title: [Amateur film: Parade of Krewe of Rex, New Orleans, February 25, 1941]
family.note: Children in costume at a parade: attitudes linked into ceremony.

family.title: Fire and Police Service
family.note: Firemen in a line with hoses: gesture drilled into a social choreography.

family.title: Structure Protection Strategies in the Wildland/Urban Interface
family.note: Three policemen standing for the camera: bodies arranged by the institution.

family.title: Bookkeeping and Accounting
family.note: An official reading from a large book: Police, Adjective's dictionary scene, meaning fixed by ceremony.

family.title: Surviving Forced Landings
family.note: A hand-drawn diagram: the chief's blackboard, procedure turned into gesture.

43.name: Cinema of the brain
43.difference: Is the set or world laid out as a map of thought (abstract floor plans, chalk-drawn spaces, landscapes as mental states), so that the screen reads as a brain rather than a place to act in?

family.title: Banks And Credits
family.note: A town plan seen from above: like Dogville's chalk-drawn village, the world as a diagram of thought.

family.title: Arteries of New York City
family.note: Branching lines across a dark field: arteries that read as neurons.

family.title: Growth of Cities
family.note: A growing street network: a city laid out like a cortex.

family.title: Heat Treatment of Aluminum, Part I
family.note: A polygonal cell network: matter organised like tissue.

family.title: Caught Mapping
family.note: A hand drawing a map: space thought as it's made.

family.title: The Eclipse
family.note: A field of stars: the identity of cosmos and brain that Deleuze names.

44.name: Lectosigns
44.difference: Does grasping the film require you to relink its images, narration and narrative yourself, because none of them links 'naturally' and no single key object resolves it?

family.title: How Man Made Day
family.note: Neon signs at night: Enter the Void's Tokyo, light that has to be deciphered.

family.title: Communications Primer, A
family.note: A page of text in the frame: reading replaces looking.

family.title: Your Movie Camera and How to Use It
family.note: A page of printed instructions: the image must be read, not simply seen.

family.title: Gift of Green
family.note: A glowing flower against black: an organic form that looks like something else.

family.title: Ask Me, Don't Tell Me
family.note: A storefront of lettering: the street as text.

family.title: Great American Chocolate Factory, The
family.note: Rows of red cones in close-up: an abstraction the eye can't settle.
